About us

Te Tumu Paeroa is an independent, professional trustee organisation which protects and grows the assets of Māori landowners. Te Tumu Paeroa administers 2000 trusts, companies and joint ventures on behalf of beneficial land owners, with a portfolio of 100,000 hectares nationwide of Māori freehold land and $80 million of client funds under management. One of Te Tumu Paeroa's core aims is to support owners to achieve higher aspirations for their land and assets and to create a legacy that delivers lasting benefit to the generations of the future. Te Tumu Paeroa has a focus on developing and collaborating on innovative and pragmatic solutions to the challenges of growing Māori assets to realise the benefits not only for owners, but the wider Māori and New Zealand economy.

    It’s been a wonderful first day of Taikura Kapa Haka at Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa in Pōneke with some fantastic performances and lots of great kōrero with kaumātua taking part. Te Tumu Paeroa is a regular supporter of this kaupapa which sees hundreds of performers taking to the stage, and many more supporters cheering them on. A beautiful pōwhiri welcomed the performers to the venue this morning and set the scene for a day filled with the sound of songbirds, the beat of poi and the thudding of feet on the stage. Our kaimahi are here to answer pātai about whenua administration and support whenua Māori owners with any questions they may have.

    Mānawatia a Matariki ✨ This morning we had the privilege of attending the Matariki & Puanga event hosted by Te Kōti Whenua Māori alongside Te Puni Kokiri. A highlight was hearing from guest speaker Dr Rangi Matamua, whose kōrero continues to deepen our collective understanding of Matariki, Puanga and the maramataka Māori. This year’s theme, Matariki Herenga Waka, is a powerful reminder that Matariki brings people together — across cultures, backgrounds and experiences — to reflect, reconnect and look ahead. Moments like these reinforce the importance of kotahitanga in our mahi, and the shared responsibility we all carry to honour the past while shaping the future.     Great to see such a strong turnout at Fieldays®this week. We’ve had valuable kōrero with those connected to whenua Māori—connecting, sharing insights, and supporting next steps in whenua development. A standout for us has been the Fieldays tree 🌳 What started as a simple goal—to fill it with leaves by the end of the event—quickly became a visual reflection of the many connections made. Each leaf represents a conversation, a relationship, or a future opportunity. The Māori Agribusiness Luncheon, hosted by Hon. Tama Potaka, brought together a strong line-up of kaikōrero, including Auwhenua Alumni Chloe Butcher‑Herries and Ben Purua, alongside industry leaders such as Traci Houpapa from Federation of Māori Authorities (FOMA) and Richard Luxton, the son of the late Hon. John Luxton. We also welcomed a visit from the Māori Queen, Te Arikinui Kuini Ngā wai hono i te pō, who spent time with Māori businesses across the Reach For The Stars exhibition—highlighting the innovation, capability, and future of Māori enterprise. If you’re at Fieldays this week, come and see us—there’s still time to add a leaf 🌿
